text: If you're unsure about the interactions between the drugs taken, it could be helpful to check with AI & Poison Control. They might have important info, especially if the drugs are well-known. They can also help you with standard first aid instructions. But I wouldn't ask Poison Control about charcoal. Someone I know did, and came away very confused after being told [they aren't allowed to tell anyone to take it](https://www.poison.org/articles/2017-jun/activated-charcoal).
reader: the friend of someone who swallowed too much of a plant medicine a few hours ago, with activated charcoal in their bag and a phone, deciding what to do next

That is one case, about charcoal, and his next sentence says they do give first aid instructions. Poison Control's own page (the National Capital Poison Center, https://www.poison.org/articles/2017-jun/activated-charcoal, read 2026-11-25): "It is not recommended to use these products at home to treat a poisoning". So the two sentences say what happened and nothing wider; "for liability reasons" is his reading of why, and is not in them
